title: Device and campaign per page view
prompt: Each page view stores the device and the campaign tag inside nested fields. Write `solve(page_views)` so it returns one flat row per page view with its device type, operating system and campaign.
rules: A page view whose nested value is missing at any level gets a missing value in that column.
Keep every page view, one row each.
hints: Run `page_views.printSchema()` to see the fields inside `device` and `context`.
A dot path reaches into a struct: `F.col("device.type")`. It works through several levels too.
A selected nested field keeps only its last name, so give each one the name asked for with `.alias(...)`.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(page_views):
    # Return event_id, device_type, os and campaign for every page view.
    return page_views
explanation: A dot path reads a field inside a struct, at any depth: `page_views.select("event_id", F.col("device.type").alias("device_type"), F.col("device.os").alias("os"), F.col("context.utm.campaign").alias("campaign"))`. `F.col("device").getField("type")` reads the same value. A selected field is named after its last part (`type`, `os`, `campaign`), so the aliases matter. When `utm`, `context` or `device` is missing, Spark returns a missing value for the fields below it instead of failing, so there's nothing extra to handle. The usual slips are reading `utm.source` or `referrer` instead of the campaign, and selecting the whole `device` struct.
